name: Grafana
tagline: Queries Prometheus, Loki and Tempo; draws dashboards, sends alerts and links signals.

howItWorks.title: Datasources as code
howItWorks.body:
YAML under provisioning/datasources defines Prometheus, Loki and Tempo.
Fixed uid values keep dashboards portable across environments.
Grafana proxies queries server-side; browsers never reach the backends.
Provisioned datasources are read-only in the UI.

howItWorks.title: Dashboards as code
howItWorks.body:
A file provider loads dashboard JSON from a mounted directory.
JSON lives in Git; changes arrive by pull request, not by clicking.
Variables and uid-bound datasources let one dashboard serve every cluster.
allowUiUpdates: false stops the UI diverging from Git.

howItWorks.title: Four golden signals
howItWorks.body:
Latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(x_bucket[5m]))).
Traffic: sum(rate(x_count[5m])) in requests per second.
Errors: 5xx rate divided by total rate.
Saturation: CPU, memory, queue depth from node_exporter.
Panels follow that order so on-call engineers read top to bottom.

howItWorks.title: Alerting
howItWorks.body:
Alert rules query a datasource, apply a threshold and hold for a duration.
Notification policies route by label to contact points.
Rules and policies provision from YAML like everything else.
Alert on symptoms users feel, not on every cause.

howItWorks.title: Trace-to-logs correlation
howItWorks.body:
Prometheus exemplars carry a trace_id on latency points.
Click an exemplar and Tempo opens that trace.
tracesToLogsV2 jumps from a span to Loki lines filtered by trace ID.
Loki derivedFields turn trace_id in a log line into a Tempo link.

howItWorks.title: What sits in front
howItWorks.body:
Users open dashboards over HTTPS, usually through the Edge reverse proxy.
Sign-in uses OIDC through generic OAuth against an identity provider such as Keycloak.
Behind a reverse proxy, set root_url, plus serve_from_sub_path if it lives under a path.
Dashboards and datasources arrive as provisioned files from Git.

howItWorks.title: What sits behind
howItWorks.body:
Grafana's server must reach each backend: Prometheus 9090, Loki 3100, Tempo 3200.
On Kubernetes, the Helm chart sidecar loads dashboards from labelled ConfigMaps.
The default SQLite database suits one instance; use PostgreSQL to run several replicas.
Contact points deliver alerts to Slack, email or any webhook.

howItWorks.title: Alternatives
howItWorks.body:
Kibana: choose it when Elasticsearch or OpenSearch is the main data store.
Datadog or other SaaS dashboards: choose them to avoid running servers.
Perses: a newer open-source dashboard project with dashboards as code.
Prometheus console or Alertmanager UI: enough for a quick check, not for dashboards.

flow: Provisioning files mount into Grafana at startup.
Datasources register Prometheus, Loki and Tempo with fixed uids.
Dashboard JSON loads from the file provider.
Panels run PromQL and LogQL through the Grafana proxy.
An exemplar on a latency point opens the trace in Tempo.
Tempo jumps from a span to its Loki logs.
Alert rules evaluate and route to contact points.

deploy.summary: Grafana OSS in Docker with Prometheus, Loki and Tempo provisioned as code, plus a golden-signals dashboard.
prerequisites: Loki and Tempo reachable, or drop those datasources

steps.title: Directory layout
steps.code:
mkdir -p provisioning/datasources provisioning/dashboards dashboards
touch docker-compose.yml

steps.title: Firewall: admin subnet only
steps.code:
# 10.0.0.0/24 = admin subnet (placeholder)
sudo ufw allow from 10.0.0.0/24 to any port 3000 proto tcp
sudo ufw status numbered
steps.note: Replace the subnet. In production publish only the TLS reverse proxy.

steps.title: Compose file
steps.code:
services:
  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana:11.1.0
    environment:
      GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_USER: admin
      GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD:?set GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD}
      GF_USERS_ALLOW_SIGN_UP: "false"
    volumes:
      - ./provisioning:/etc/grafana/provisioning:ro
      - ./dashboards:/var/lib/grafana/dashboards:ro
      - grafana-data:/var/lib/grafana
    ports: ["3000:3000"]
networks:
  default:
    name: monitoring
volumes:
  grafana-data: {}
steps.note: Export GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD first; compose refuses to start without it. The network is shared with Prometheus.

steps.title: Datasources with correlation
steps.code:
apiVersion: 1
datasources:
  - name: Prometheus
    uid: prom
    type: prometheus
    access: proxy
    url: http://prometheus:9090
    isDefault: true
    jsonData:
      exemplarTraceIdDestinations:
        - name: trace_id
          datasourceUid: tempo
  - name: Loki
    uid: loki
    type: loki
    access: proxy
    url: http://loki:3100
    jsonData:
      derivedFields:
        - name: TraceID
          matcherRegex: 'trace_id=(\w+)'
          url: '$${__value.raw}'
          datasourceUid: tempo
  - name: Tempo
    uid: tempo
    type: tempo
    access: proxy
    url: http://tempo:3200
    jsonData:
      tracesToLogsV2:
        datasourceUid: loki
        filterByTraceID: true
        spanStartTimeShift: '-5m'
        spanEndTimeShift: '5m'
steps.note: Save as provisioning/datasources/ds.yml. Loki and Tempo must resolve at these hostnames; adjust URLs.

steps.title: Dashboard provider
steps.code:
apiVersion: 1
providers:
  - name: file-dashboards
    folder: Platform
    type: file
    allowUiUpdates: false
    options:
      path: /var/lib/grafana/dashboards
steps.note: Save as provisioning/dashboards/provider.yml. Grafana rescans the path periodically.

steps.title: Golden signals dashboard
steps.code:
{
  "uid": "golden-signals",
  "title": "Golden Signals",
  "schemaVersion": 39,
  "time": {"from": "now-1h", "to": "now"},
  "panels": [
    {"id": 1, "type": "timeseries", "title": "Latency p95 (s)", "gridPos": {"x": 0, "y": 0, "w": 12, "h": 8},
     "datasource": {"type": "prometheus", "uid": "prom"},
     "targets": [{"refId": "A", "expr": "histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_bucket[5m])))"}]},
    {"id": 2, "type": "timeseries", "title": "Traffic (req/s)", "gridPos": {"x": 12, "y": 0, "w": 12, "h": 8},
     "datasource": {"type": "prometheus", "uid": "prom"},
     "targets": [{"refId": "A", "expr": "sum(rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count[5m]))"}]},
    {"id": 3, "type": "timeseries", "title": "Error ratio (5xx)", "gridPos": {"x": 0, "y": 8, "w": 12, "h": 8},
     "datasource": {"type": "prometheus", "uid": "prom"},
     "targets": [{"refId": "A", "expr": "sum(rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{status=~\"5..\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count[5m]))"}]},
    {"id": 4, "type": "timeseries", "title": "Saturation: CPU cores used", "gridPos": {"x": 12, "y": 8, "w": 12, "h": 8},
     "datasource": {"type": "prometheus", "uid": "prom"},
     "targets": [{"refId": "A", "expr": "sum(rate(process_cpu_seconds_total[5m]))"}]}
  ]
}
steps.note: Save as dashboards/golden-signals.json. Metric names assume Spring Boot Micrometer.

steps.title: Alert rule provisioning
steps.code:
apiVersion: 1
groups:
  - orgId: 1
    name: slo
    folder: Platform
    interval: 1m
    rules:
      - uid: high-error-ratio
        title: High 5xx ratio
        condition: C
        for: 5m
        noDataState: OK
        execErrState: Error
        labels: {severity: critical}
        annotations: {summary: "5xx ratio above 2 percent"}
        data:
          - refId: A
            datasourceUid: prom
            relativeTimeRange: {from: 600, to: 0}
            model:
              expr: sum(rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count[5m]))
              instant: true
              refId: A
          - refId: C
            datasourceUid: __expr__
            model:
              type: threshold
              expression: A
              conditions:
                - evaluator: {type: gt, params: [0.02]}
              refId: C
steps.note: Save as provisioning/alerting/rules.yml (already mounted). Route with a notification policy.

steps.title: Start
steps.note: Change the password; keep it in a secret store.

verify: Provisioning errors: docker compose logs grafana | grep -i provisioning
pitfalls: Dashboards without a fixed datasource uid break when imported elsewhere.
Edits to a provisioned dashboard made in the UI are lost on restart.
Default SQLite blocks running two replicas; use PostgreSQL.
Exemplars need the app to emit them and Prometheus exemplar storage on.
Alerting on every cause pages humans for noise; alert on symptoms.
The 'No data' state silently hides outages; set noDataState deliberately.
An admin password in a Compose file ends up in Git; use secrets.
keyPoints: Grafana queries datasources; it stores no metrics itself.
Datasources, dashboards and alerts are provisioned from Git.
Four golden signals: latency, traffic, errors and saturation.
Exemplars and derived fields jump from metric to trace to logs.
quickDeploy: Define Prometheus, Loki and Tempo datasources.
Load the golden-signals dashboard from JSON.
Start and check the datasources API.
osiNote: HTTP application: queries backends and serves dashboards over HTTPS.
production: Provision everything as code; disable UI edits on shared dashboards.
Store state in PostgreSQL and run two replicas behind a load balancer.
Put SSO and TLS in front; no anonymous admin, no sign-up.
Back up the database and dashboard repo; restore-test quarterly.
Alert on datasource errors and scrape Grafana's own /metrics.
